雑.meaning: Halfway up a <part>tree</part>, <part>nine</part> <part>sparrow</part> stallholders run a junk sale, one per branch: a single sock, a cracked teacup, a kazoo, half a map, a spoon with a bite out of it. Nothing matches anything else. The sign nailed to the trunk just says <kanji>miscellaneous</kanji>.
雑.on: It's the oddest stall in the whole ba<sound>za</sound>ar, and the dust off the junk makes the smallest sparrow sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
雑.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>!' cheeps a chick, digging a toy <sound>jee</sound>p out from under the socks: everything here is all mixed in together.

帯.meaning: A tightrope walker's costume is a mess: a <part>comb</part> stuck in her hair, a <part>blanket</part> round her shoulders, a <part>towel</part> round her hips. Before she steps onto the rope, her coach ties the whole lot in place with one long silk <kanji>sash</kanji>.
帯.on: Out of silk for the second knot, the coach whips off his own <sound>tie</sound> and wraps it round her waist as well.
帯.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps, halfway across, as the sash slips up to her neck, and she wears it as a scarf to the end.

携.meaning: A tiny sailor <part>sparrow</part> packs for a voyage: a pocket-sized <part>anchor</part>, and a <part>folding ruler</part> that snaps down small enough to tuck under one wing. Everything she owns folds up and flies with her. Her whole life is <kanji>portable</kanji>.
携.on: Under the other wing she carries a little birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke, folded neatly in half.
携.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!' she chirps, landing, and unpacks a picnic she brought all the way: a yu<sound>zu</sound> and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

鶏.meaning: The star of the puppet show is a <part>marionette</part> of a <part>bird</part> that clucks, scratches the stage and lays a wooden egg. Halfway through, the strings snap, but it keeps strutting about on its own. It was never a puppet at all: it's a real <kanji>chicken</kanji> who loves the stage.
鶏.on: For its encore, it pecks a whole <sound>ca</sound>ke to crumbs in front of the front row.
鶏.kun: At the curtain call it drops to one <sound>knee</sound>, the crowd gasps '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and it flaps off to roost on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole among the <sound>ree</sound>ds.

集.meaning: Every evening at six, one <part>sparrow</part> lands on the town's last <part>tree</part> and rings a tiny bell. From every gutter and chimney, thousands more pour in until the branches sag like a feathered umbrella. It's the sparrows' town meeting, and they all <kanji>gather</kanji> before the vote.
集.on: The last one to arrive paddles in late, rowing an old <sound>shoe</sound> down the gutter like a boat.
集.kun: They all crowd round the oldest sparrow to hear her speak, and she sneezes: '<sound>Ah</sound>… <sound>tsu</sound>!'

形.meaning: At sports day for cats, a tabby sails over a <part>hurdle</part> but snags her <part>whiskers</part> on the bar. When she lands, they've bent into a perfect star. Next jump, a heart; then a square. Every hurdle gives her whiskers a new <kanji>shape</kanji>.
形.on: Her prize is a <sound>ca</sound>ke baked in the shape of a fish.
形.kun: On the podium she holds up a <sound>ca</sound>rp, purrs '<sound>Ta</sound>-da!' and bites a wedge of <sound>chee</sound>se into the shape of a star.

指.meaning: A ship's cook has lost her ladle, so she stirs the soup with the ship's <part>anchor</part>. To check it's <part>delicious</part>, she dips in her smallest <kanji>finger</kanji> and licks it.
指.on: The anchor sends hot soup splashing everywhere, so the crew duck behind a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
指.kun: The secret ingredient: she squeezes in a <sound>yu</sound>zu, then fishes out a <sound>bee</sound> that fell in, with the same finger.

議.meaning: A council of owls sits round an old stump while a mouse on trial waits. Each owl makes a long <part>speech</part> about <part>justice</part>, then another, then another. Nobody votes; they just keep weighing every word until dawn. This is <kanji>deliberation</kanji>.
議.on: Inside the stump, one huge wooden <sound>gea</sound>r turns a single notch after every speech, slow as a snail.

師.meaning: In a dusty gym, an old woman hangs a <part>towel</part> over <part>one</part> crossbar and props up a <part>pole</part> with a cheeky <part>mouth</part> painted on it. 'Hit the pole, not the towel,' she says, and flicks it flat without looking. She's the <kanji>expert</kanji> everyone has come to learn from.
師.on: Her students hide behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld, but she flicks that flat too.
師.kun: In the old war, they say, she beat a whole army armed with an <sound>ee</sound>l, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

臣.meaning: A tiny butler lives in the bottom <part>drawer</part> of the king's desk. Whenever the king opens it, he pops up and bows, holding out a pen, a seal, a mint, whatever is needed. He has served the crown for forty years: the most loyal <kanji>retainer</kanji> in the land.
臣.on: Before every bow he nibbles a knob of <sound>gin</sound>ger to keep his old back from creaking.

緊.meaning: At the royal banquet, a <part>servant</part> hangs a giant <part>pretzel</part> above the king's head on a single <part>thread</part>. The thread stretches thin and starts to quiver. Nobody breathes, nobody chews. The whole room is <kanji>tense</kanji>.
緊.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher darts through the window and snatches the pretzel a second before the thread snaps.
緊.kun: The servant pulls the next knot so tight that a <sound>shee</sound>p in the corner faints from the strain.

式.meaning: A carpenter hammers a <part>stake</part> into the corner of her <part>workbench</part> and hangs her hat on it, tilted just so. Pencil behind one ear, sawdust swept into a heart. Even mending a wobbly chair, she does it with <kanji>style</kanji>.
式.on: <sound>She</sound> locks her toolbox every night with a golden <sound>key</sound> on a silk ribbon.

共.meaning: Two friends carry a stretcher: a <part>pole</part> in each hand, <part>two</part> crossbars between them, their legs spread like an <part>eight</part> as they shuffle along. If either lets go, the whole thing drops. They can only move <kanji>together</kanji>.
共.on: The two friends carry the stretcher all the way to <sound>Kyo</sound>to, singing the first half of its name together in one long, slow breath.
共.kun: On the stretcher lies a wooden <sound>to</sound>tem pole, and a <sound>mo</sound>le rides on top, waving to the crowd.

字.meaning: A <part>child</part> climbs onto the <part>roof</part> with a bucket of paint and draws one giant letter across the tiles, big enough for planes to read. Nobody knows what language it's from. It's a single mystery <kanji>character</kanji>.
字.on: Down below, a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p parks under it so the driver can copy it onto his map.
字.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps a rug seller at the ba<sound>za</sound>ar down the street: it's the very same letter woven into all his rugs.

情.meaning: A robot gets a screen fitted on its chest. Its <part>heartbeat</part> line glows <part>blue</part> when it's sad, pink when it's happy, and flickers green when it's jealous of the toaster. The robot has just discovered <kanji>feelings</kanji>.
情.on: It first sobs blue tears watching a lost <sound>jo</sound>ey hop back into its mother's pouch.
情.kun: When it cries, the toaster just says '<sound>Nah</sound>,' and goes on toasting a <sound>sa</sound>rdine. Not a scrap of sympathy.

報.meaning: In a town with no paper, the news comes baked. Each dawn the baker presses a rubber <part>stamp</part> into every <part>pretzel</part>: sugared ones for stories of <part>happiness</part>, salty ones for trouble. You eat the morning <kanji>report</kanji> with your coffee.
報.on: When the oven catches fire, she sprays the whole batch with a garden <sound>ho</sound>se, and the news comes out soggy.
報.kun: To reward her, a cow outside gives a grateful '<sound>Moo</sound>', and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the clock to sing.

在.meaning: A dreamer plants a <part>pole</part> in a mound of <part>soil</part>, nails <part>one</part> board across its top and paints a <part>slash</part> on it, a signpost to nowhere. People walk for miles just to touch it and nod: yes, it's real. The sign's only job is to <kanji>exist</kanji>.
在.on: Each visitor taps out a tune along the board with two sticks, as if it were a <sound>xy</sound>lophone.
在.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' sigh the visitors, patting the post, 'so it really is there.'

任.meaning: Before her trip, Grandma hangs her <part>spindle</part> on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door and tells her grandson: 'Keep spinning while I'm gone. The whole village's wool depends on you.' It's the first big job she has ever chosen to <kanji>entrust</kanji> to him.
任.on: A <sound>nin</sound>ja creeps in each night to check that he's still spinning.
任.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, a <sound>ca</sound>rp!' he yells, pulling a fish out of the wool basket. Leave it to him: he'll sort it out.

命.meaning: Under a striped <part>umbrella</part>, a stern clerk sits at a desk with <part>one</part> ruler, a tight <part>mouth</part> and a rubber <part>stamp</part>. You hand her your life story; she reads it without a word and thumps the stamp down. No arguing: that is your <kanji>fate</kanji>.
命.on: The stamp says 'hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze', and in you go, with no map.
命.kun: Deep inside, an <sound>ee</sound>l, a <sound>no</sound>mad and a mouse nibbling <sound>chee</sound>se have been lost for years, but they're all still very much alive.

収.meaning: Every morning a street seller hangs fresh <part>pretzel</part> twists up and down a tall <part>pole</part>. Every night the pole is bare and his hat is full of coins. He sells nothing else. Those pretzels are his whole <kanji>income</kanji>.
収.on: He stores every coin he earns stuffed inside one old <sound>shoe</sound> under his bed.
収.kun: At closing time he counts the hat: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' Someone has paid him with a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

例.meaning: At the lost-property office, coats hang in a strict <part>rank</part> along the wall. The very first <part>coat hook</part> holds one coat folded perfectly, buttons done up, a flower in the lapel. A sign above it says: hang yours like this. It's the <kanji>example</kanji> for every coat after it.
例.on: Even the aquarium's gliding <sound>ray</sound> hangs its little coat there, exactly as the sign shows.
例.kun: The clerk holds each new coat up beside it and compares: this scruffy one's like a <sound>ta</sound>co, that stiff one's like a <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

限.meaning: At the edge of the race track stands a stiff-legged <part>robot</part> with a <part>pennant</part>. Go one mile faster than the sign and it clanks into the road, waving the flag: no further. It's there to enforce the speed <kanji>limit</kanji>.
限.on: The robot's name, <sound>Gen</sound>, is stamped on its chest, and in forty years it has never let anyone past.
限.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in a racing car shifts <sound>gea</sound>r, but even it can't go past the limit.

加.meaning: A <part>muscle</part>-bound chef stirs a pot the size of a bathtub while a tiny critic's <part>mouth</part> keeps saying 'More!' In go a pinch of salt, then a whole onion, then a tuba. Every time the mouth opens, he has to <kanji>add</kanji> something.
加.on: Finally he tosses in a live <sound>ca</sound>rp, and it splashes the critic from head to toe.
加.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the kitchen clock to drop in one feather, and the critic cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

投.meaning: At the village games, a shy <part>maiden</part> in a long skirt steps up to the line, curtseys, and swings a ship's <part>anchor</part> round her head. Off it sails, over the barn and the church spire. Nobody has ever seen anyone <kanji>throw</kanji> like that.
投.on: She spins round so fast before letting go that she stubs her <sound>toe</sound> on the line.
投.kun: Her prize is a hot <sound>na</sound>an, and she throws that too, straight over the crowd.

権.meaning: At the park pond, one <part>sparrow</part> stands at the end of a <part>diving board</part> nailed to an old <part>tree</part>, blowing a whistle. Ducks, swans and even the dog wait in line until it says jump. Tiny as it is, it holds all the <kanji>authority</kanji>.
権.on: When the whistle blows twice, even the guard dog slinks back into its <sound>ken</sound>nel.
権.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps a <sound>mo</sound>le, as the sparrow drops a lead sinker off the board, plop, down to the <sound>ree</sound>f of stones at the bottom: a weight.

経.meaning: Across the desert rolls a <part>tumbleweed</part>, trailing a <part>thread</part> that unwinds a long scroll behind it. Every inch is covered in tiny holy verses, and a monk walking after it chants each line as it passes. The wind is reading him a <kanji>sutra</kanji>.
経.on: When the scroll runs out, the monk finds a little rice <sound>ca</sound>ke tied to the very end.
経.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n follows the monk for a thousand miles, pecking at each line as they pass through village after village.

古.meaning: On a tortoise's birthday cake the candles won't fit, so the baker writes a giant <part>ten</part> and adds zeros all the way round the edge. The tortoise opens its wrinkly <part>mouth</part>, puffs, and blows out one candle an hour. It's very, very <kanji>old</kanji>.
古.on: Its only friend at the party is a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala who is nearly as ancient.
古.kun: Afterwards they nap on one worn-out <sound>fu</sound>ton, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> tucks them both in.

能.meaning: At the talent show, a stubby <part>teapot</part> waddles on stage with a <part>spoon</part> stuck on each side like arms. It pours itself a cup, stirs it, juggles three sugar lumps and catches them in its lid. The judges give it top marks for <kanji>ability</kanji>.
能.on: The runner-up is a garden <sound>gno</sound>me, whose only talent is standing very still.
能.kun: For its encore, it pours a perfect swirl of <sound>yo</sound>gurt into every judge's cup: done really well.

護.meaning: Every night, a <part>falconer</part> climbs the city wall and gives a short <part>speech</part> to her hawk: 'Watch the hen houses, the kittens and the baker's cat.' Then the hawk circles the town till dawn. Its job is to <kanji>safeguard</kanji> everyone asleep.
護.on: To see in the dark, the hawk wears a tiny pair of swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles.
護.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! A <sound>mo</sound>le!' squeaks a kitten, and the hawk drops down to stand guard beside her.

看.meaning: A babysitter sneaks off to the kitchen, but leaves a glove propped on the cot: a <part>hand</part> with a big googly <part>eye</part> sewn on the palm. Whenever the baby sits up, the eye wobbles and the baby lies back down. Even from the kitchen she can <kanji>watch over</kanji> the baby.
看.on: She tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the glove so the baby has something sweet to smell.
看.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands on the cot rail as backup, keeping a look-out too.
